summary: `runBackendCli` only calls `installShutdown` after `createStdioBridge` resolves. While connect or startup catch-up is still running, stdin is not being read, so closing it ends nothing. A plugin whose connect keeps a handle open (for example a reconnecting socket) and never finishes leaves an orphaned bridge running forever.
failure: I ran the compiled `runBackendCli` with a plugin whose `connect()` never resolves but arms a `setInterval` (standing in for a client retrying its connection), with stdin from /dev/null or a pipe that closes after 0.3 s. Expected: the bridge exits on EOF. Actual: still alive at the 5 s timeout (exit 124) in both cases, and it would stay alive until connect resolves. The `readableEnded`/`destroyed` checks only run once the attach has finished.
remediation: Detect parent death during attach without reading stdin. Resuming stdin early would discard the `initialize` bytes the MCP transport has not subscribed to yet. Options: record `process.ppid` at start and poll for a change during attach (exit when the process has been reparented), or attach the MCP transport before `plugin.connect` (a reorder in transport/stdio-bridge, owned by another target).

remediationCheck.reliesOn: Node's `process.ppid` changing to the subreaper/init pid when the parent dies (POSIX; not reliable on Windows). The reorder option relies on `buildBridge`'s `abortIfToreDown` latch.
remediationCheck.newlyRejects: With the ppid poll: a bridge deliberately launched by a short-lived wrapper that exits after spawning (e.g. `nohup`-style double fork) would now exit during attach.
remediationCheck.testsThatWouldFail: none found. I looked at cli/shutdown.test.ts (it drives `installShutdown` only), bridge-sqlite/src/cli.test.ts (EOF after 'bridge up') and conformance/test/published-bins.test.ts (--help/--version exit codes).
remediationCheck.hidesOrFixes: Fixes the orphan. A connect that hangs while the parent is alive still hangs; that is the plugin's own connect-timeout problem.
remediationCheck.interleavings: Parent dies before attach (ppid poll fires and exits; nothing to tear down beyond the process). Parent dies after attach (existing EOF listener fires; the once-guard must also cover the poll so it does not exit mid-shutdown). Both at once: the poll should be cleared when `installShutdown` arms.

summary: `installShutdown` registers SIGINT/SIGTERM listeners, which removes Node's default terminate behaviour. Its once-only guard then ignores every later signal. Also bound the teardown in `runBackendCli` with `Promise.race([bridge.shutdown(), deadline])` so a hung disconnect cannot outlive it.

summary: parley_live_status reports 'not-delivering' (and the tool text tells the agent 'the live path is dead... you should say so') for a healthy push path whenever the agent pulls backlog that this boot's catch-up did not warm. The no_start_catchup blocker assumes on-start catch-up warms everything the reconciling read will return. The warm marker and the catchup.limit horizon both break that assumption, even in the default configuration.
failure:
Reproduced with a FakePlugin (working subscribe), live_push.enabled=true.
(a) Cold boot with 5 messages and catchup.limit=2. Catch-up warms the newest 2. The agent's since-less parley_fetch_recent returns 5. Result: {status:'not-delivering', pushed:0, reconciled:3}.
(b) Boot 1 with 3 messages (agent never reads; marker is written at the head). Shutdown, one new message, then boot 2 with default limit 100. Catch-up pages only from the marker (drained=1, so no head read). The agent reads from its position: old0..old2 plus new. Result: {status:'not-delivering', pushed:0, reconciled:3}.
In both cases no live traffic has occurred yet, so the correct verdict is 'no-traffic'.
remediation: Count a reconciled message only when the read that returned it started at a cursor known to be at or past this boot's live boundary. Catch-up's final warmedTo per topic is the boundary. The cursors known to be past it are the boundary itself, the nextCursor of any page read from such a cursor, and the cursor of any pushed message. The LiveDeliveryLedger would hold that per-topic set (bounded by the topic count). Pages starting from older or unknown cursors contribute nothing. summary: Refresh rotation deletes the presented token, and nothing remembers it. A replayed rotated token is just an unknown token (invalid_grant), and the grant stays live. summary: The shared LISTEN connection only learns it is dead from a socket 'end'. A peer that stops answering while keeping the socket open (hung primary, a TCP proxy or pooler mid-failover) leaves push silently dead with no reconnect and no redrive: the bridge believes it is subscribed. The listener sends nothing, so query_timeout never applies. TCP keepalive (connection.ts KEEPALIVE_DELAY_MS, documented as making such a peer 'an error, not silence') never fires while an intermediary's kernel still ACKs, and takes about 11 minutes on Linux defaults otherwise.

remediation: Add an unref'd listener heartbeat, e.g. every 15s run `SELECT 1` on the adopted listener; SOCKET_BOUNDS' query_timeout already bounds it. summary: rejoinAfterReconnect re-drives only the rooms still in `joined`. A subscribed room whose re-entry failed earlier is dropped from `joined` by ensureJoinedRoom's catch and only logged by redriveJoin. One example is the occupancy-loss ladder firing while the stream was down, where send() rejects. A reconnect therefore never re-enters that room, and live push for the topic stays dead even though the stream came back. README promises 'After a reconnect the plugin re-sends the join presence for every room it had entered — subscribed or catch-up-only'.
failure: FakeXmpp repro: subscribe(t), then a kick with status 307 arms the ladder (200–400 ms). send() rejects for 700 ms (stream down), so the ladder re-join fails and the room is removed from joined. send() is restored and 'online' is emitted (reconnect). Result: 0 new join presences; joined.has(room)=false, subscriptions.has(room)=true. fake.deliver(room,'after-reconnect') reaches the handler: [] (expected ['after-reconnect']).
remediation: In rejoinAfterReconnect, re-drive the union: `const rooms = new Set([...this.forgetAllRooms(), ...this.subscriptions.keys()]); for (const room of rooms) void this.redriveJoin(room, 'reconnect');`

remediationCheck.hidesOrFixes: Fixes the reconnect hole. remediationCheck.interleavings: (1) Ladder timer pending at reconnect: the reconnect re-drive joins first, and the timer later finds the cached promise and does nothing. summary: A cursor from a re-provisioned stream is answered with the newest `limit` messages of the new incarnation. Its nextCursor sits at the tail, so every new-incarnation message below that window is skipped for good, even though all of them are newer than anything the caller has read. Seam clause 3 says fetchRecent is COMPLETE. The comment's claim that the fallback does not 'silently skip everything the new incarnation holds below it' is false whenever the new incarnation holds more than `limit` messages.
failure: Reproduced live on nats:2.10. Post 'old-1' and catch up, which persists cursor A-1. Then `nats stream rm` and post 150 new messages; the plugin re-provisions as incarnation B. Draining fetchRecent from A-1 page by page (default limit 100) returns only new-51..new-150, so new-1..new-50 are lost. Any `catchup.limit` smaller than the new incarnation loses messages the same way; the shipped example code-agent-b.yaml uses limit 50.
remediation: When `restarted` is true, read the new incarnation from its start instead of falling into the since-less backwards walk. Use the since path with startSeq = Math.max(firstSeq, 1): `pull(stream, topic, startSeq, Math.min(limit, tailSeq - startSeq + 1), tailSeq)` followed by `pageOrWait(read, startSeq)`. Keep the `messages === 0` → waitOrNothing branch as it is. Apply the same rule to a legacy bare cursor above lastSeq.

remediationCheck.reliesOn: NatsPulls.pull, and pageOrWait's `messages.at(-1)?.cursor ?? this.cursorAt(stream, Math.max(startSeq - 1, 0))`, which mints a replayable empty-page cursor below startSeq. Also the existing `const startSeq = Math.max(since.seq + 1, firstSeq, 1)` branch shape.

I expect the plain and long-poll rows to still pass, because 40 is below limit 100. resource-live 'catch-up from the pre-removal cursor recovers' posts only one message after the removal, so it still passes.
remediationCheck.hidesOrFixes: Fixes the loss for a cursor whose incarnation token mismatches. A legacy bare cursor at or below the new lastSeq is still unjudgeable and still skips (documented).

testUpgrade: Parameterize the cursor-input re-provision table over (new-incarnation length) × (limit), including lengths larger than the limit. summary: The since-less backwards walk concatenates each lower window under the higher ones. If a LOWER window's pull is cut short (idle close, expiry or slow link, the documented truncation modes), the page holds that window's first few messages plus the higher windows' messages, and nextCursor jumps over the unread middle. The existing short-read tests use 5 contiguous records under one window, so the multi-window case is never graded.
failure: Reproduced with the shared fake. Records are at seqs 1..10 and 20, limit 8, and the fake's yieldLimit is 3. The walk reads window [13..20] and gets m20, then window [1..12], which is truncated to m1,m2,m3. The page is [m1,m2,m3,m20] with nextCursor at seq 20, so a full replay never returns m4..m10.
remediation: Use the walk only to find the window's START, then do one ascending pull from that start with `limit`, so truncation can only cut the top and the cursor of the last returned message is safe. Alternatively, have pull() report whether it provably reached `top`, and when a lower window is unproven, return only that window's messages, dropping the higher ones, which the next catch-up re-reads upward.

remediationCheck.reliesOn: pull()'s `if (read >= want || m.seq >= tailSeq) break` termination, and pageOrWait's last-returned-message cursor.
remediationCheck.testsThatWouldFail: Not run. window.test.ts 'a page costs what the page holds… the read scales with the hole, not the depth' may bound `yielded` or the pull count, and an extra ascending pull adds up to `limit` yields.
remediationCheck.hidesOrFixes: The start-then-ascend variant fixes the skip. A cold-start page that is truncated returns older messages rather than the newest, which the seam permits.

testUpgrade: Cross cursor.test.ts's completeness table (complete/partial/empty yieldLimit) with sparse multi-window histories (holes or foreign tails that force at least 2 walk windows) and limits from 1 up to the history depth. That re-creates the id collision with the new incarnation's own sequences that the incarnation exists to prevent, and core's dedup then drops real messages.

summary: requireSendableBody runs /[\p{White_Space}\u001c-\u001f]+$/u over the whole caller-supplied body before any length check. V8 backtracks this quadratically on a long whitespace run that does not reach the end. Core puts no cap on parley_post/reply content, so one call freezes the single-threaded bridge for every session, including remote/chat mode.
failure: plugin.post(topic, h, ' '.repeat(200_000) + 'x') → the event loop is blocked for about 16s inside String#replace before any request is sent (100k → 3.9s, 40k → 0.64s; the cost grows with the square of the run length). The same regex runs again at line 154. SERVER_STRIPPED_TOPIC_EDGE is also quadratic ('ctx-'+' '.repeat(1e5)+'x' → 4.8s), but core's 64-character MAX_MATCH_INPUT bounds pattern-admitted topics.
remediation: Replace both uses of SERVER_STRIPPED_BODY_TAIL with a linear backward scan: `let end = content.length; while (end > 0 && BODY_TAIL_CHAR.test(content[end - 1]!)) end--;`, where BODY_TAIL_CHAR is the single-character /^[\p{White_Space}\u001c-\u001f]$/u. Use the same helper for the 'which edge' test at line 154. Apply the same shape to the trailing half of SERVER_STRIPPED_TOPIC_EDGE.

summary: Once a socket has stayed up for STABLE_CONNECTION_MS, the reconnect ladder resets to rung 0. After that it can spend IDENTIFYs on 1s, 2s, 4s… rungs again until the next stable window. summary: During a Socket Mode rotation the old socket stays `this.ws`. If it closes while the replacement's apps.connections.open is still in flight, its close handler sets `wsReady = undefined` and wipes out the pending attempt. A concurrent ensureSocket (e.g. subscribe on another topic) then starts a second dial in parallel, and two sockets stay established for the rest of the session.
failure: Reproduced (critic-repro.test.ts 'rotation…'). Setup: subscribe CA, setLatency('apps.connections.open', 300), send disconnect{reason:'warning'}, dropOldestSocket() 50 ms later, then subscribe CB. Result: 2 dials and liveSockets=2 that persist. The expected result is 1 dial and 1 socket. Two event sources feed one channel, which breaks the 'ONE connection feeds a channel' basis of ascending delivery and uses up one of the ~10 per-app connections.
remediation: In the `reason === 'warning'` branch of routeEnvelope, retire the rotating socket as the current one: set `this.ws = undefined` next to `this.wsReady = undefined`. The old socket's close then takes the `this.ws !== ws` early return, and the reconnect loop that is already running stays the only owner of re-establishing the socket.

remediationCheck.reliesOn: openSocket close handler: `if (this.host.stopped() || this.ws !== ws) return;`, plus reconnect() looping `while (!this.host.stopped() && this.host.session() === session)` until ensureSocket resolves.
remediationCheck.newlyRejects: none at the API. Behaviour change: the rotated-out socket's close no longer calls noteConnectionEnded or resets the dial ladder.
remediationCheck.testsThatWouldFail: None. I applied the change and ran all 19 slack test files: 1088/1088 passed, including envelope-robustness 'disconnect reason drives the rotation' and connection-lifecycle rotation rows.
remediationCheck.hidesOrFixes: Fixes it. As far as I traced, rotation is the only path where a served socket is `this.ws` while a newer attempt is pending, because a new attempt only starts once wsReady is undefined.
remediationCheck.interleavings: (a) old socket closes while reconnect is waiting out its cooldown: ignored, loop dials once. (b) old socket closes during the replacement's apps.connections.open: ignored, a concurrent subscribe joins wsReady. (c) replacement fails while the old socket is in grace: the loop keeps retrying, and the grace timer's close is ignored. (d) two subscribes in the window both join the same wsReady.

The existing rotation rows only drop the old socket after liveSockets===2, which is why this was missed.

summary: The live path forwards every routed envelope as-is. Nothing enforces the seam's clause that the handler fires 'in ascending cursor order, never twice'. An envelope Slack redelivers (retry_attempt) is handed to the handler again, and so is an older ts arriving after a newer one. The link's own comment admits nothing orders anything, and the ack-failure comment relies on redelivery.
failure: Reproduced: push ts2, then ts1, then ts2 again (retry_attempt:1) on one channel. The handler receives ['…000002','…000001','…000002']: out of order and duplicated. A realistic trigger is the rotation grace closing the old socket (CLOSING state): acks sent there are dropped silently by ws while routing still happens, so Slack redelivers on the new socket.
remediation: Enforce the invariant in one place. Keep a per-route high-water `lastTs` and deliver only when `compareTs(event.ts, route.lastTs) > 0`, then advance it. Anything rejected this way is left to catch-up, as the lossy contract allows.

remediationCheck.newlyRejects: A live event whose ts is <= the last delivered ts on that route, e.g. a Slack redelivery or a late event during rotation overlap. It is still acked, and catch-up returns it.
remediationCheck.testsThatWouldFail: Observed: hostile-input.test.ts 'slack ts range … > live push: every ADMITTED ts reaches the handler, every REJECTED one is dropped, socket survives'. It pushes GENERATED in non-ascending order and requires all of it delivered, which encodes the violation. It needs to push in compareTs order. All 1087 other tests passed.
remediationCheck.hidesOrFixes: Fixes the seam clause for both duplicates and reordering. It does not make the ack reliable on a CLOSING socket. That needs no fix, since redelivery is then dropped harmlessly.
remediationCheck.interleavings: Two sockets during rotation feeding one route: whichever event arrives first sets lastTs, and an older one from the other socket is dropped. A re-subscribe replaces the route object, which resets lastTs. That is acceptable because delivery restarts at the tail.

summary: A leftover `<store_path>.lock` naming THIS process's own pid is treated as a live holder, so a bridge that restarts under the same pid (PID 1 in a container with a persistent volume, or any reused pid) can never reopen its store. failure: Write `${process.pid}\n` to `<store>.lock`, then `new ObservedStore(store)` with no other in-process holder. It throws "is already claimed by process <own pid> ... If no such process is running, remove ...", even though the process it names is the one asking. Reproduced. In a Docker deployment, an OOM-kill followed by a restart leaves the bridge unable to connect until an operator deletes the lock by hand.
remediation: Keep a module-level registry of lock paths this process holds (realpath of the directory plus the basename). Grade liveness as `pid === process.pid ? HELD.has(path) : processExists(pid)` everywhere a holder is adjudicated: claim(), replaceStale() (which re-asks processExists) and takeBreak(). A break token naming our own pid at entry is necessarily a leftover, because a take-over runs synchronously.

summary: A getUpdates 429 whose stated retry_after exceeds the poll call's deadline (about 35s at the default 25s timeout) makes net-util end the call immediately. remediation: Carry the server-stated wait on the rejection: have net-util's overDeadline branch put a `retryAfterMs` field on the HttpStatusError (a net-util change, not core). On status 429, pollUpdates waits max(retryAfterMs, 500) with a delay that is cut short when isCurrent() goes false. Without a stated wait, back off exponentially up to a cap rather than 500ms flat.

remediationCheck.reliesOn: net-util index.ts throws `new HttpStatusError(opts.label, 429, stated && overDeadline ? 'upstream asked for ...' : ...)`. Today that carries the wait only in prose, so a field must be added. The poll loop reads the status via statusOf(err).

The 'still rate limited after N attempts' branch has no stated wait and still needs the exponential fallback.
remediationCheck.interleavings: disconnect() during the wait: the generation is bumped and the abortable delay resolves early, so the loop exits at the isCurrent() check. summary: sleepUnlessStopped arms setTimeout(ms) with the server's full wait. Past 2^31-1 ms Node wraps the timer to 1 ms. fetchWithRetry accepts any finite deadlineMs, so a stated wait that fits the deadline is retried immediately. That breaks the module's central promise ('never retry sooner than the vendor asked'). attempt.ts's armableDelay guards this exact overflow for the request timer, but the backoff timer is unguarded.

Reproduced against a real node:http server. The README promises such a wait is 'honoured in full, however long'.
remediation: Make the backoff timer overflow-safe. In sleepUnlessStopped, record `until = Date.now() + ms` and arm setTimeout(min(remaining, 2**31-1)), re-arming on fire until `until` is reached, keeping `cancels` pointed at the live timer. Apply the same to the exported `delay`. Alternatively (simpler, but it rejects inputs) refuse deadlineMs > 2**31-1 under the existing `→ deadline:` label, since any wait that fits the deadline is then armable.

failure: A bot invited with View Channels and Send Messages but without Read Message History. fetchRecent({topic}) returns {messages:[], nextCursor:'0'} on a channel with history. The subscribe check reports nothing and core's catch-up reads it as an empty topic.

If it is non-null, issue one `GET …/messages?limit=1`; an empty answer warns that the bot appears to lack Read Message History and catch-up will see nothing. Warn rather than reject, because a channel whose messages were all deleted gives the same signal.

Real Telegram strips leading and trailing whitespace from message text (and rejects empty text). Unverified: there is no live Telegram token in this environment.

summary: When a Telegram group is upgraded to a supergroup, the old chat id stops receiving messages and the bot gets a service message carrying `migrate_to_chat_id`. contentOf() returns undefined for it (it is not text, a caption or a MEDIA_KIND), so it is dropped without a diagnostic. A chat_map topic pointing at the old id goes silently dark on the inbound path, while the new chat's traffic piles up as an unserved chat that nothing reads. Posts fail loudly (400 'group chat was upgraded'), but subscribe and fetchRecent give no signal.
failure: chat_map {ops: '-12345'}; the group is upgraded to -100987...; Telegram sends {message:{chat:{id:-12345}, migrate_to_chat_id:-100987...}}. It is ingested as nothing and reported nowhere, and fetchRecent('ops') stays empty for good. Traced through contentOf/ingest. The upstream behaviour comes from the Bot API docs and was not reproduced live.
remediation: In the poll loop (or ingest), detect `migrate_to_chat_id` / `migrate_from_chat_id` on a message and report a throttled diagnostic naming the old and new chat ids and telling the operator to update chat_map.
